title: European Union Update — May 10, 2026
summary: Hungary's Péter Magyar was sworn in as Prime Minister on Europe Day (May 9), ending Viktor Orbán's 16-year dominance and raising the EU flag over Budapest's parliament for the first time since 2014 — a seismic shift that removes the bloc's most persistent internal veto. The EU-Mercosur Interim Trade Agreement entered provisional application on May 1, activating the world's largest trade deal by population across 700 million people after 25 years of negotiations. Trump escalated transatlantic tensions on May 7 by setting a July 4 deadline for EU ratification of the 2025 Scotland trade deal or face 'much higher' tariffs, with significant gaps remaining in negotiations. The ECB held its deposit rate unchanged at 2.00% on April 30 despite internal debate on a potential hike due to energy price pressures. The 8th European Political Community Summit in Yerevan (May 4) and the first-ever EU-Armenia bilateral summit marked Armenia's strategic pivot toward Europe.
